name: TikTok LIVE Studio — Streaming
description: Keeps a live broadcast's capture and encode pipeline ahead of background work: the studio itself gets AboveNormal priority and the high-performance GPU, while browsers, sync clients and music players are pushed below it. Nothing is suspended, so no browser source, upload or chat client stops mid-stream.
notes: Nothing is suspended: a broadcast must not lose a browser source, an upload or a voice call mid-stream, so competing apps are only pushed to BelowNormal.

Hardware encoding (NVENC on NVIDIA, AMF on AMD, Quick Sync on Intel) is the single biggest CPU saving while streaming, but it is chosen in the studio's own output settings — no profile can change another app's encoder.
Discord is deliberately not listed. Lowering a voice client's priority trades audio latency for a little CPU, which is the wrong trade while you are live.
The session stays applied while the studio is running, so alt-tabbing to chat does not end it; every priority and the GPU preference are restored when it exits or the session is stopped.
